stem: The trochlear nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
fact: The trochlear nerve innervates the superior oblique muscle.
mnemonic: SO4: superior oblique is supplied by CN IV.
finding: Source page displays superior oblique as correct.

stem: The spinal accessory nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
fact: The spinal accessory nerve supplies the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.
mnemonic: CN XI turns the head and shrugs the shoulders: SCM and trapezius.
finding: Source page displays sternocleidomastoid and trapezius as correct.

stem: The facial nerve divides into its five terminal branches at which of the following sites:
options: At the lateral corner of the eye
At the lower border of the mandible
fact: The facial nerve divides into its five terminal branches within the parotid gland.
mnemonic: Inside the parotid, VII splits into five terminal branches.
finding: Source page displays within the parotid gland as correct.

stem: Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates from the medulla.
The glossopharyngeal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity via the jugular foramen.
The glossopharyngeal nerve is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex.
The glossopharyngeal nerve innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle.
The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies parasympathetic fibres to the parotid gland.
fact: The glossopharyngeal nerve is the afferent limb of the gag reflex; the vagus nerve is the efferent limb. Therefore, the statement that CN IX is efferent is incorrect.
mnemonic: IX in, X out: glossopharyngeal senses the gag and vagus contracts the pharynx.
finding: Source page displays the third statement as the incorrect one.

stem: A 64 year old man presents to ED complaining of diplopia. The image below shows the patient's eyes gazing straight ahead. Which of the following cranial nerves is affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: Abducens nerve palsy causes a convergent squint, inability to abduct the eye, and horizontal diplopia.
mnemonic: LR6: lateral rectus is supplied by CN VI; failure lets the eye turn in.
finding: Source page and explanation display abducens nerve as correct.

stem: The facial nerve exits the posterior cranial fossa through which of the following:
fact: The facial nerve exits the posterior cranial fossa through the internal acoustic meatus before entering the facial canal.
mnemonic: VII and VIII enter the temporal bone through the internal acoustic meatus.
finding: Source page displays internal acoustic meatus as correct.

stem: A 54 year old man presents to ED complaining of difficulty chewing. On examination, you note he has loss of muscle bulk over the masseter muscle and loss of power opening the jaw. He also has loss of tactile sensation involving the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Which of the following cranial nerves is most likely affected:
fact: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve supplies the muscles of mastication and general sensation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue via its lingual branch.
mnemonic: V3 chews and feels: mastication plus anterior-tongue sensation.
finding: Source page displays mandibular nerve as correct.

stem: Regarding the mandibular nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The mandibular nerve enters the infratemporal fossa between the tensor veli palatini muscle and the lateral pterygoid muscle.
The mandibular nerve exits the cranium through the foramen ovale.
The mandibular nerve supplies sensation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
The mandibular nerve innervates the orbicularis oculi.
The mandibular nerve has both motor and sensory function.
fact: Orbicularis oculi is a muscle of facial expression supplied by the facial nerve, not the mandibular nerve.
mnemonic: V3 is motor and sensory, but VII closes the eyelids.
finding: Source page displays innervation of orbicularis oculi as the incorrect statement.

stem: Regarding the oculomotor nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The oculomotor nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The oculomotor nerve innervates all of the extraocular muscles.
The oculomotor nerve innervates the dilator pupillae muscle.
The oculomotor nerve passes through the lateral part of the cavernous sinus.
The oculomotor nerve enters the orbit through the optic canal.
fact: The oculomotor nerve travels in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. It is a motor nerve and supplies sphincter pupillae through parasympathetic fibres, not dilator pupillae.
mnemonic: III is motor, travels in the cavernous sinus, and enters through SOF.
finding: Source page displays passage through the lateral cavernous sinus as correct.

stem: A 29 year old man has sustained a significant head injury. On examination it is noted that his uvula is deviated to the right. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
fact: A unilateral vagus lesion causes the uvula to deviate away from the affected side. With left vagal weakness, the intact right side pulls the uvula rightward.
mnemonic: Vagus weakness pulls the uvula away: left lesion, right deviation.
finding: Source page displays left vagus nerve as correct.
